paper.title_en: Development of a Polarized H^+/D^+ Ion Source at IMP
paper.abstract_en: Polarized particle beams provide experimental access to the spin degree of freedom in nuclear and particle physics research. Utilizing spin-dependent observables, a multitude of experiments that are not achievable with conventional beam can be conducted. As part of the research and development efforts for key technologies prototyping for electron-ion collider in China (EicC), an intense spin-polarized ion source (SPIS) has been developed at the Institute of Modern Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences (IMP, CAS). At present, SPIS can produce polarized proton (deuteron) beams with a current of 1 mA and a beam polarization of about 80% with a pulse duration of 100 microseconds at a repetition rate of 5 Hz. SPIS adopts an improved Lamb-shift polarimeter (LSP), with which the polarization of the beams extracted from the ion source can be measured directly. The integration of SPIS into high-intensity heavy ion accelerator facilities (HIAF) will enable the production of high-energy polarized ion beams, providing a powerful tool for cutting-edge physics research.
